The '''2022–23 Eredivisie''' was the 67th season of the [[Eredivisie]], the premier football competition in the [[Netherlands]]. It began on 5 August 2022 and concluded on 28 May 2023. As the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]] started on 20 November, the last round before stoppage was held on 12–13 November. The league resumed games on 6 January.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|date=9 December 2021|title=Speeldagenkalender '22/'23: eredivisie stopt 13 november en hervat op 6 januari|url=https://www.ad.nl/nederlands-voetbal/speeldagenkalender-22-23-eredivisie-stopt-13-november-en-hervat-op-6-januari~a59a3994/|access-date=27 May 2022|website=ad.nl|language=nl-NL}}</ref>

[[Feyenoord]] became the champions in round 32, beating [[Go Ahead Eagles]] 3–0 at  [[De Kuip]] in [[Rotterdam]] on 14 May 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-05-14 |title= Feyenoord voor de 16e keer kampioen van Nederland|url=https://eredivisie.nl/nieuws/feyenoord-voor-de-16e-keer-kampioen-van-nederland/ |access-date=2026-03-15 |website=Eredivisie |language=NL}}</ref>

==Teams==
[[FC Emmen|Emmen]] (promoted after a one-year absence), [[FC Volendam|Volendam]] (promoted after a thirteen-year absence) and [[Excelsior Rotterdam|Excelsior]] (promoted after a three-year absence) were promoted from the [[2021–22 Eerste Divisie]]. [[Willem II Tilburg|Willem II]] (relegated after eight years in the top flight), [[PEC Zwolle]] (relegated after ten years in the top flight), and [[Heracles Almelo]] (relegated after seventeen years in the top flight) were relegated to the [[2022–23 Eerste Divisie]].
